platform_selection_rule: The two numerically lowest rail-platform numbers at each of four fixed stations in the development GTFS. Exact IDs remain fixed; no date-specific substitution. Roma Street starts at platforms 3 and 4, not the similarly named busway platforms.
primary_selection_rule: All ordered interstation combinations of the eight fixed platform IDs, expanded at five fixed departure offsets. Equal query weights, including unavailable source stops or paths; no filtering by disruption or recovery outcome.
control_rule: Score the original OD20 requests separately under the plans optimized for the primary census. Never pool denominators or double-weight duplicate queries across cohorts.
scenario_selection_rule: All actual adjacent rail movements whose endpoint station names are different members of the fixed Fairfield-Central section, including express movements. Close both directions for two hours. Existing engine semantics cancel every complete source trip crossing a selected segment during the interval. No source bus movement may be selected.
candidate_rule: Use the existing affected-corridor candidate selector on nominal primary inputs, at most three source-supported paired bus patterns. Expand each at the four fixed activation offsets, at most twelve candidates. One hypothetical bus and a full two-hour duty per candidate, unchanged source running times and five-minute terminal turns. Freeze nominal identities across sensitivity levels.
duty_horizon_limit: Duties end 09:40-10:25, after the hypothetical closure ends09:30:05. Count their full two-hour cost. Decompose improvements by whether the recovered query arrives after the closure ends; neither timetable running times nor initial vehicle positioning establish actual dispatch feasibility.
simple_policy_rule: Among nominal relevant paired patterns, rank by unique source bus trips departing within the two-hour closure interval, descending, then pair ID. Dispatch the most frequent feasible pair at the fixed activation offsets up to the budget, retaining infeasibility reasons. This is service frequency, not passenger demand; do not claim the legacy affected-bus heuristic applies to rail-only cancellation.
impacted_cohort_rule: A nominal baseline-reachable primary query whose disrupted capped duration exceeds its baseline capped duration. Determine once before recovery; retain this same cohort for every budget and stress. Always display full primary and separate control denominators too.
example_rule: Show the fixed Fairfield platform 2 to Central platform 1 query departing at the decision cutoff, including null outcomes; never choose the example by recovery benefit.
interpretation: Exploratory development and separately frozen confirmation of a hypothetical broad rail outage. Recorded provider predictions and schedule fallback are not measured arrivals. No calibrated passenger demand, vehicle capacity, fleet positioning, financial return or real-world savings are inferred. Missing walking access is retained as a limitation. More severe disruption and a new primary workload do not replace or retroactively improve v1.0.0 findings.
